slides.say: A supply of hay is enough for two hundred identical sheep for nine days. Each sheep eats the same constant amount per day. For how many days would that supply feed ninety sheep?
at: A supply of hay is enough

slides.say: So the hay stays the same, and the number of sheep changes. They ask for the number of days.
at: They ask for the number of days

slides.say: We'll solve it in three different ways. This time I'll start, on purpose, with an estimate. It helps us understand the question, because this one isn't simple.
Fewer sheep eat the same hay more slowly. So the hay lasts longer, more than nine days.
And really, all four choices are more than nine days. So the question is how many more.
Ninety is close to a hundred, and a hundred is exactly half of two hundred. Half is the easiest to work with, so let's go through it first.
Half of two hundred is a hundred. Half the sheep make the hay last twice as long. Nine times two is eighteen days.
at: Half of two hundred is a hundred

slides.say: But we have ninety sheep, a bit fewer than a hundred. Fewer sheep make the hay last longer. So a bit more than eighteen days.
at: a bit fewer than a hundred

slides.say: So eighteen, choice number two, is out. And fifteen, choice number one, is fewer than eighteen, so it's out too.

Twenty and twenty-seven are left. Ninety sheep are only ten fewer than a hundred, a small change. So the days grow only a little above eighteen. Twenty-seven is nine days more than eighteen, half as much again. That's far too much, so twenty-seven is out.
So the estimate alone picks twenty, choice number three. Now let's see two exact ways.
[pause] Now let's plug in numbers. We start again from the givens. The amount each sheep eats isn't given. So let's say each sheep eats one unit of hay a day.
Two hundred sheep for nine days. Two hundred times nine is one thousand eight hundred units. That's all the hay.
Ninety sheep eat ninety units a day.
One thousand eight hundred divided by ninety. We can drop a zero from both numbers. A hundred eighty divided by nine is twenty. So twenty days.
Let's check it. Ninety times twenty is one thousand eight hundred. That's all the hay.
So twenty days. That's choice number three, just like the estimate.
[pause] And this is even a team question, once we see who the team is. We start again from the givens.
The sheep are the workers. Their job is eating. The hay is the work, and the hay doesn't change. So the work is one supply in both rows.
The question mark is in the time. So the V joins two hundred, one and nine. We divide by the rest, one and ninety.
at: So the V joins two hundred

slides.say: Two hundred over ninety is twenty ninths, because we divide both by ten.
Twenty ninths times nine. The nine cancels the ninth, and that leaves twenty days.

The hard part was to see who the team is. Sometimes a supply gets used up at a constant rate, like hay, water or fuel. Then the ones who use it are the team. And the supply is the work. If you don't see it, the estimate and plugging in numbers work too.
Choice number three is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number three is our answer
